reasons: Claimed status is compliant with no redline and no comment, which is the expected output shape; the rendered paragraphs are unchanged from the originals, so there is no risk of an invalid or directionally wrong edit.

The cited § 4(c) grant genuinely reaches at least the fallback on its material terms: it is royalty-free, non-exclusive and perpetual, contains no revocation or at-will termination mechanic (confirmed by the 'no at-will revocation remains' check), and its use scope is broad ('in connection with Company's business operations') rather than narrowed to internal use.

The failed 'affiliates covered by the licence' regex is a phrasing-variant false negative rather than a substantive gap: the unconditional 'right to grant a sublicense' gives Clear Capital a self-executing path to extend the licence to affiliates and contractors, which is at least as favourable as the fallback's 'affiliates covered on written notice' and defeats the walk-away trigger of exclusion with no path to add them.

The two shortfalls from preferred wording (no express 'irrevocable' label; successor transfer left to the mutual § 10 consent-not-unreasonably-withheld clause) are correctly treated as minor sub-elements noted in the rationale rather than redlined, consistent with the playbook's classification semantics.

The grant runs in favour of our party (Company = Clear Capital, Customer side), so flagging it as a deviation would have been over-flagging; retaining it as compliant internal evidence is the right disposition.
